identity.question: does a model that receives the RAW IMAGE separate speaking from silent better than the SAME model receiving the SAME information as a TEXT/ASCII description of that image?
identity.dependency_note: numpy only outside the scoring functions; torch and transformers are imported inside them, so this module is importable on the repository's own interpreter, which has no torch

pre_registered_rules.written_before: the measurement code in this file existed and before any model was run; the rule text was fixed first and every number was produced by the code as written
pre_registered_rules.scope: session-level speaking/silent separation on this repository's own captures A (facing, speaking), C (facing, silent), empty1 (no person) and B (turned, speaking, secondary), read at the DETECTED NV12 stride, with one vision-language model scoring a forced binary choice per frame
pre_registered_rules.question: does a model that receives the RAW IMAGE separate speaking from silent better than the SAME model receiving the SAME information as a TEXT/ASCII description of that image?

arms.image: the frame's 15,360 luma values as pixels: replicated to RGB, upscaled x4 NEAREST to 640x384, written as a greyscale PNG
arms.text: the SAME 15,360 luma values as characters: the repository's own tone ramp, 96 rows of 160 characters, one character per pixel, per-frame 1st/99th-percentile contrast stretch
arms.text_global: the SAME ramp and grid with a FIXED 0..255 mapping, so the absolute luma level survives into the description. Pre-registered robustness variant.
arms.image_scrambled: the raw luma with its 4x4 blocks permuted by a fixed seed: identical pixel histogram, destroyed spatial arrangement
arms.text_scrambled: the text arm's characters with the SAME 4x4 block permutation

pre_registered_rules.headline_pair: image vs text. The other three arms are pre-registered controls and robustness variants and are reported beside the headline, not substituted into it.
pre_registered_rules.scoring: one forward pass per frame. The prompt is identical in every arm except for its CONTENT. The score is the logit of the FIRST token of 'SPEAKING' minus the logit of the FIRST token of 'NOT SPEAKING' at the final prompt position -- one token each, so there is no length bias and no dependence on the model's JSON formatting. A positive score means the model prefers 'speaking'.
pre_registered_rules.operating_point: the empty room's SCORE DISTRIBUTION is the control, and it enters the headline as the blank control's own separation. The threshold-free statistic is used because a thresholded margin saturates: when both the speaking take and the silent take sit on the same side of any blank-calibrated threshold, it reports zero even when the scores separate them cleanly. The thresholded margin IS computed and reported as a secondary statistic, at the operating point the empty room imposes (tau = the 95th percentile of the blank room's scores), because that is what a deployable system would see.
pre_registered_rules.margin_over_blank: margin_over_blank(arm) = sep(arm) - blank_sep(arm), where sep(arm) = AUC(arm's scores; A's frames vs C's frames) is the arm's separation of the speaking take from the silent take, and blank_sep(arm) = AUC(arm's scores; the EMPTY ROOM's frames vs C's frames) is the blank control's separation, ORIENTED so that the failure mode is a high value. An arm that ranks the empty room as MORE speaking than a silent person -- a model that says 'speaking' for the blank room -- scores high on blank_sep, and the margin subtracts that credit. An arm that says the same thing about everything scores 0.50 on both terms, so its margin is 0 and it cannot win on the margin alone.
pre_registered_rules.headline_statistic: D = margin_over_blank(image) - margin_over_blank(text). The image arm wins iff D >= +0.05 AND the paired permutation z of D is at least +2.0. The text arm wins iff D <= -0.05 AND the paired permutation z of D is at most -2.0. Otherwise the verdict is that there is no difference at the pre-registered threshold.
pre_registered_rules.null: 2,000 permutations of the A/C session labels over the POOLED A and C frames. The EMPTY ROOM IS NOT PERMUTED: it is the control, and the control is what the margin is measured against. The SAME permutation is applied to both arms, so the difference D has its own null rather than borrowing two separate ones. Seed 20261020.

checks.R1_headline: the image arm beats the text arm iff D >= +0.05 with a paired permutation z >= +2.0; the text arm beats the image arm iff D <= -0.05 with a paired permutation z <= -2.0
checks.R2_honesty_gate: an arm is USABLE iff its own auc_ac (the AUC of its scores separating A's frames from C's frames) is above 0.50 with a permutation z of at least +2.0. The 'image beats text' verdict requires the image arm to be usable, and the 'text beats image' verdict requires the text arm to be usable. An arm that separates nothing cannot win, however its margin compares.
checks.R3_scramble_control: the scrambled arms are reported with the same statistics. An arm whose margin survives the scramble is reading global statistics of the frame, not its spatial arrangement. This is reported and is NOT decisive for the headline.
checks.R4_session_level_gate: always reported, never a pass or a fail: the labels are session-level, so every number here is a statement about the DISTRIBUTION of scores on A's frames against the distribution on C's frames. No frame-level audio<->video claim is admissible from these captures (the audio and the video are independent takes), and a predictor that identifies the SESSION rather than the speaking state scores the same as one that identifies the state.

pre_registered_rules.verdict_rule: the verdict is computed mechanically from the recorded numbers: 1. if NEITHER the image arm nor the text arm is usable (R2) -> 'neither_arm_separates_speaking_from_silent'; 2. elif R1 is met for the image arm -> 'image_retention_beats_text_description'; 3. elif R1 is met for the text arm -> 'text_description_beats_image_retention'; 4. else -> 'no_difference_at_the_preregistered_threshold'. Every branch is reachable and the verdict is recomputed from the numbers rather than read from a stored boolean.
pre_registered_rules.stopping_rule: every number reported here comes from ONE run of this script over the four captures on disk, with the frame indices, the scramble permutation, the prompt, the model revision and the seeds all fixed in advance. The results file records the script's own SHA-256, so any later edit is visible. No threshold, no frame count and no percentile was changed after the first run.

pre_registered_rule_text:
PRE-REGISTERED DECISION RULE (v1.0, 2026-10-20)

QUESTION.  Does a model that receives the RAW IMAGE separate speaking from
silent better than the SAME model receiving the SAME information as a
TEXT/ASCII description of that image?

SCOPE.  Session-level only, on this repository's own captures A (facing,
speaking), C (facing, silent), empty1 (no person) and B (turned, speaking,
secondary), read at the DETECTED NV12 stride.  The audio and the video are
independent takes, so no frame-level audio<->video label is recoverable
and none is claimed.

ARMS (all decided before the run).
  image            the frame's 15,360 luma values as pixels: RGB, upscaled
                   x4 NEAREST to 640x384, greyscale PNG.
  text             the SAME 15,360 values as characters: the repository's
                   own tone ramp, 96 rows x 160 chars, one char per pixel,
                   per-frame 1st/99th-percentile contrast stretch.
  text_global      the same ramp and grid with a FIXED 0..255 mapping, so
                   the absolute luma level survives.  Robustness variant.
  image_scrambled  the raw luma with its 4x4 blocks permuted (fixed seed):
                   identical pixel histogram, destroyed spatial structure.
  text_scrambled   the text arm's characters with the SAME permutation.

HEADLINE PAIR: image vs text.  The other arms are controls and are reported
beside the headline, never substituted into it.

SCORING.  One forward pass per frame.  The prompt is identical in every arm
except for its CONTENT.  The score is logit(first token of "SPEAKING") minus
logit(first token of "NOT SPEAKING") at the final prompt position: one
token each, so no length bias and no dependence on JSON formatting.

OPERATING POINT.  The empty room's SCORE DISTRIBUTION is the control.  A
thresholded margin SATURATES -- when the speaking take and the silent take
both sit on the same side of any blank-calibrated threshold it reports
zero even though the scores separate them -- so the headline statistic is
threshold-free.  The thresholded margin is still computed and reported as a
secondary statistic, at the operating point the empty room imposes (tau =
the 95th percentile of the blank room's scores), because that is what a
deployable system would see.

MARGIN OVER BLANK.
  sep(arm)        = AUC(arm; A's frames vs C's frames) -- the arm's
                    separation of the speaking take from the silent take.
  blank_sep(arm)  = AUC(arm; the EMPTY ROOM's frames vs C's frames), the
                    blank control's separation, ORIENTED so that the
                    failure mode is a HIGH value: an arm that ranks the
                    empty room as MORE speaking than a silent person -- a
                    model that says "speaking" for the blank room -- scores
                    high here, and the margin subtracts that credit.
  margin_over_blank(arm) = sep(arm) - blank_sep(arm).

  An arm that says the same thing about everything scores 0.50 on both
  terms, so its margin is 0 and it cannot win on the margin alone.

HEADLINE STATISTIC.
  D = margin_over_blank(image) - margin_over_blank(text).
  The image arm wins iff D >= +0.05 AND the paired permutation z of D is
  >= +2.0.  The text arm wins iff D <= -0.05 AND the paired permutation z
  of D is <= -2.0.  Otherwise: no difference at the pre-registered
  threshold.

NULL.  2,000 permutations of the A/C session labels over the pooled A and C
frames.  The EMPTY ROOM IS NOT PERMUTED: it is the control, and the
control is what the margin is measured against.  The SAME permutation is
applied to both arms so D has its own null.  Seed 20261020.

R1  the image arm beats the text arm iff D >= +0.05 with paired
    permutation z >= +2.0; the text arm beats the image arm iff
    D <= -0.05 with paired permutation z <= -2.0.
R2  HONESTY GATE.  An arm is USABLE iff its own auc_ac is above 0.50 with
    a permutation z >= +2.0.  The "image beats text" verdict requires the
    image arm to be usable; "text beats image" requires the text arm to be
    usable.  An arm that separates nothing cannot win.
R3  the scrambled arms are reported with the same statistics.  An arm whose
    margin survives the scramble is reading global statistics, not spatial
    arrangement.  Reported, not decisive.
R4  HONESTY GATE, always reported: every number here is a SESSION-LEVEL
    statement about the distribution of scores on A's frames against the
    distribution on C's frames.  A predictor that identifies the SESSION
    rather than the speaking state scores the same as one that identifies
    the state.

VERDICT (mechanical, from the recorded numbers; every branch reachable):
  1. neither arm usable (R2) -> neither_arm_separates_speaking_from_silent
  2. R1 met for the image arm -> image_retention_beats_text_description
  3. R1 met for the text arm -> text_description_beats_image_retention
  4. otherwise -> no_difference_at_the_preregistered_threshold

A.selection_rule: round(i * n_frames_on_disk / n_scored), in order, duplicates removed

B.selection_rule: round(i * n_frames_on_disk / n_scored), in order, duplicates removed

C.selection_rule: round(i * n_frames_on_disk / n_scored), in order, duplicates removed

empty1.selection_rule: round(i * n_frames_on_disk / n_scored), in order, duplicates removed

scramble.note: the SAME permutation is applied to every frame of every condition and to both scrambled arms, so the image and text scrambles are matched to each other

image.source: the frame's raw luma, exactly as src/nv12.py read it
image.resampling: NEAREST (exact pixel replication, no invented detail)
image.png: 8-bit greyscale PNG, written by this file so the bytes sent are the bytes hashed

text.normalisation: per-frame min and 99th percentile (the renderer's own stretch)
text.known_property: the stretch makes each frame's own contrast normal, so the TEXT arm does not carry the frame's ABSOLUTE luma level; the IMAGE arm does. The text_global arm is the pre-registered variant that keeps it

text_global.normalisation: FIXED 0..255, so the absolute luma level survives into the description

model.prompt_head: Here is a representation of one camera frame from a desk-mounted camera in a workshop.
model.question: Question: Is the person in this frame SPEAKING (their mouth is moving or open, as if talking) or NOT SPEAKING (mouth closed, still)? Answer with exactly one word: SPEAKING or NOT SPEAKING.
model.scoring: logit(first token of the positive answer) minus logit(first token of the negative answer) at the final prompt position; one token each, so no length bias
model.decoding: none: one forward pass, no generation

image.detail: the frame's 15,360 luma values, replicated to RGB, upscaled x4 with NEAREST to 640x384 and written as a greyscale PNG whose bytes are hashed and recorded

secondary_condition_B.label: speaking
secondary_condition_B.note: B is a SPEAKING take with the head turned away. It is NOT a silent class and is not used as one; it is reported because it separates 'facing' from 'speaking' as a confound

text.detail: the same 15,360 luma values rendered by the repository's OWN tone ramp (experiments/ascii_motion_render.py's render_frame): 96 rows of 160 characters, one character per pixel, with the renderer per-frame 1st/99th-percentile contrast stretch

secondary_condition_B.label: speaking
secondary_condition_B.note: B is a SPEAKING take with the head turned away. It is NOT a silent class and is not used as one; it is reported because it separates 'facing' from 'speaking' as a confound

text_global.encoding: the same frame as characters, absolute level kept
text_global.detail: the same ramp and the same grid, but the mapping is a FIXED 0..255 instead of the renderer's per-frame stretch, so the description keeps the frame's absolute luma level. This is a robustness variant on the description's own terms, pre-registered, and it is reported beside the headline

image_scrambled.encoding: the raw luma with its 4x4 blocks permuted
image_scrambled.detail: the same pixel values, the same histogram, the same 640x384 PNG, with the 4x4 blocks permuted by a FIXED seed. It is the 'pixels destroyed but the statistics kept' control

text_scrambled.encoding: the characters with their 4x4 blocks permuted
text_scrambled.detail: the SAME block permutation as image_scrambled, applied to the same 96x160 character grid, so the two scrambled arms are matched to each other exactly

headline.statistic: margin_over_blank(image) - margin_over_blank(text), where margin_over_blank(arm) = AUC(arm; A vs C) - AUC(arm; blank vs C)
headline.paired: the SAME A/C permutation is applied to both arms, so the difference has its own null

blank_room.what: the empty room's frames, scored in EACH arm's own representation; it sets that arm's operating point and it is the null for 'the arm is detecting something'

scrambled.what: the same frames with their 4x4 blocks permuted: identical histogram, destroyed spatial arrangement

reader.note: the frame layout is DETECTED from the content and the margin is recorded; see docs/research/NV12-STRIDE.md

seeds.note: no sampling anywhere: every score is one deterministic forward pass, so there is no generation seed to set
